transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

What brought me in is I can’t shake this feeling that people at work, even some of the vendors, are tracking what I buy and messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid. My supervisor shows me reports that don’t really prove it, but I still feel like something’s going on.
Have you ever heard voices, whispers, or sounds that other people around you couldn't hear?

Sometimes, yeah. In the stockroom, or driving back from a vendor meeting, I hear a man’s voice like he’s right behind me saying, “Move faster, Scott,” or laughing at my picks. I turn around and there’s nobody there.
How long have you been experiencing these concerns about people tracking you and hearing that voice?
I’d say it’s been about ten months now. The suspicious stuff and hearing that voice started around the same time.
Over these past ten months, have you been feeling persistently down, depressed, or unable to enjoy things?

I don’t know if I’d call it depressed, but on my days off I just sit in my apartment scrolling through sneaker drops and don’t really care about any of it. Friends text me about volleyball or gallery nights, and I just avoid answering because it feels like too much work.
Do you have any diagnosed medical conditions or ongoing physical health problems?
No, not that I know of. I haven’t been diagnosed with any physical health problems.
Have there been times over these past ten months when your mood and interest in things felt completely normal, but you were still hearing the voice or feeling tracked?

Yeah. There was a calmer stretch where I was sleeping more normally and didn’t feel like I was running the whole market or anything. But for a few weeks then, I still thought people were tracking what I was buying, and I kept hearing the voice in the stockroom.
You mentioned feeling like you were running the market—have there been times when you felt unusually energized, overly confident, or needed much less sleep than usual?
Yeah. There’ve been plenty of weeks where I only sleep three or four hours and wake up feeling wired, ready to go. It feels like lying in bed is just wasting time I could be using to make moves.
During those weeks when you felt wired and full of energy, did you also feel depressed, tearful, or hopeless at the same time?
I’m not really sure. When I’m that wired, I mostly just notice the energy and wanting to keep going.
